subtitle: Lesson 27 · Wait Statistics & Bottleneck Analysis

eyebrow: The headline buffer pool health metric
code:
SELECT object_name, counter_name,
       cntr_value AS ple_seconds
FROM sys.dm_os_performance_counters
WHERE object_name LIKE '%Buffer Manager%'
  AND counter_name = 'Page life expectancy';
caption: Average seconds a page survives before eviction. Not a wait-stats DMV.

code:
Old rule (small-RAM era):
  PLE < 300s = bad

Modern reality:
  judge PLE against ITS OWN TREND
  on that specific server

A sudden drop from a stable
baseline matters more than any
absolute number.
caption: There is no single universal healthy PLE number anymore.

eyebrow: When memory grants themselves queue up
code:
SELECT wait_type, waiting_tasks_count,
       wait_time_ms, max_wait_time_ms
FROM sys.dm_os_wait_stats
WHERE wait_type = 'RESOURCE_SEMAPHORE';
caption: Sorts and hash joins need a memory grant before they can even run.

subtitle: Usually the client's problem, not the server's.
